dialogues.speaker: Estella
dialogues.text: The hearth in your home has been burning brightly lately, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: And the balances in yours have been working hard, haven't they?

dialogues.speaker: Manet
dialogues.text: My hearth is strong, and the firewood, sufficient. As for the balances, I don't need 'em. It's not like I'll miss those one or two pieces of vegetables at the market, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Estella
dialogues.text: You'd best be careful. If the flames leap onto the opera house carpet, they'll put your hearth out while fighting the fires.

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: Ooh, very scary. But can you guarantee that the opera house would survive said flames?

dialogues.speaker: Manet
dialogues.text: Nah, the fire in my house won't reach the opera house. It's way too far away!

dialogues.speaker: Estella
dialogues.text: ...So, have those flames been staying put?

dialogues.speaker: Estella
dialogues.text: I'm not doing that. Just tell me.

dialogues.speaker: Manet
dialogues.text: I bet they're behaving themselves indeed. Where can they go, anyway?
